# Deck Style Notes

## Typography

Slides use one typeface family in two weights. Titles are set in the heavy weight at 36 points, body text in the regular weight at 20 points, and nothing smaller than 16 points appears anywhere, including chart labels. Line length stays under 60 characters. These rules exist so a slide can be read from the back of a room without squinting.

## Colour

The palette has one dark ink, one paper tone and one accent. The accent marks the single most important number on a slide and appears nowhere else. Charts use the ink for the data and a light grey for the grid. No gradients, no shadows, no stock photos. When a slide needs a second colour, the answer is a second slide.

## Layout rules

Every slide has a title that states a claim, not a topic. One idea per slide. Numbers cite their source note in the footer, so a reviewer can trace them; for the test stand deck that source is [[Test Stand Plan]]. Margins are 48 points on all sides and nothing touches the edge. A slide that breaks a rule is fixed, not excused.

## Common mistakes

The mistakes we see most often are a title that names a topic instead of a claim, two accent colours on one slide, a chart with a legend when a direct label would do, and a number that does not match the plan. The weekly review in [[Weekly Log 2026-09]] lists which mistakes appeared that week so the rules can be sharpened. Word meanings are in [[Glossary]].
